title: The Cell
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Onion skin and a cheek cell (scraped with a clean ice-cream stick by the learner's own hand) under the school microscope, stained with iodine by the teacher. Where there is no microscope, use labelled drawings and photographs. The magnification sum is done with the numbers printed on the lenses.

skills.key_step: The child names the parts seen under a light microscope (cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus; plus cell wall, large vacuole and chloroplasts in plant cells), gives each its job and compares plant and animal cells.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how to use and care for laboratory apparatus.
floor.question: Where do you read a measuring cylinder?
floor.answer: at eye level, at the bottom of the curve

representations: onion and cheek cells under a microscope
steps: Both: membrane (controls what enters and leaves), cytoplasm (where work happens), nucleus (controls the cell).
Plant only: cell wall (support), large vacuole (sap), chloroplasts (make food).

board.do: Draw a box-shaped cell and a round cell.

board.say: Does this one have a cell wall?

board.do: Wait for "no, it is an animal cell".
Ask the child to label the parts of both.

misconceptions.ask: Which cell is box-shaped and stiff?
misconceptions.repair: Only plant cells have a cell wall.

misconceptions.ask: Which part is green and makes food?
Do animals make their own food?

listen_for: the membrane is only the shape
misconceptions.ask: What lets water and food into the cell?
misconceptions.repair: The membrane controls what enters and leaves.

checks.question: Name two parts found in plant cells but not in animal cells.
checks.answer: any two: cell wall, chloroplasts, large vacuole

checks.question: What does the nucleus do?
checks.answer: controls the activities of the cell

skills.key_step: The child works out the total magnification by multiplying the eyepiece and objective magnifications, and knows the image, not the cell, is enlarged.
representations: the numbers printed on the microscope lenses
a hand lens over a printed letter
steps: Read the objective number (x4, x10, x40).
Say: the image is that many times bigger.
contexts: a hand lens on a leaf

board.do: Draw a microscope with x10 on the eyepiece and x40 on the objective.

misconceptions.ask: Does the second lens enlarge the first lens's image?
Does the letter change size without the lens?

checks.question: The eyepiece is x10 and the objective is x10. What is the total magnification?
The eyepiece is x5 and the objective is x40. What is the total magnification?
